after.note:
A canon stands here where no act read for this record names the title it belongs
to. That is a statement about what was read and not about the Eastern Code,
which is divided into thirty titles.
after.title: The Code as a whole, for canons this record does not place more finely

after.designation: Titulus XXVI > Caput I > Articulus I
after.note:
cann. 1357-1377. NAMED BY THE ACT THAT SUBSTITUTED IT: Mitis et misericors Iesus
decrees that Title XXVI, chapter I, article I of the Eastern Code, on cases for
declaring the nullity of a marriage, cann. 1357-1377, be substituted entire.
[Latin delivery, line 61.]
after.title: Cases for declaring the nullity of a marriage

after.note:
NAMED BY THE ACT THAT REFORMED IT: Vocare peccatores says it is reforming
twenty-two canons from Title XXVII together with can. 1152. [Latin delivery,
line 44.] It does not print the Title's canon range, so no range is written
here.
after.title: Penal law: delicts and penalties

edges.parent_basis:
The constitution names all four of the partial codifications in one parenthesis,
in order, as what the Apostolic See promulgated of the draft: `quattuor Litteris
apostolicis motu proprio datis (Crebrae allatae sunt, Sollicitudinem Nostram,
Postquam Apostolicis Litteris et Cleri sanctitati) promulgavit`. An act that
names what it completes has drawn its own edge, and the edge is drawn to the
last of the four.
